description: Entity types and relation types for ontology-guided extraction on 2WikiMultiHopQA, derived from Wikidata property constraints (SCRUM-17). A listed type admits its narrower types. The ontology supplies types and relations only; it has no composition rules (D2).

excluded_constraint_classes.reason: Registers, certifications, licences, and survey methods.
Non-human organisms, breeds, and taxa; the 2Wiki relations hold between people, works, organizations, and places.
A condition or a journey, not a place, listed as a place of detention.
Abstract cultural kinds that appear only as subjects of country of origin or founded by; 2Wiki uses those relations for works and organizations.

classes.label: figure that may or may not be fictional
fictional human formerly considered to be historical

excluded_constraint_classes.reason: Fictional, mythical, legendary, and hypothetical classes. 2Wiki answers come from Wikipedia articles about real subjects; a fictional or mythical entity is still typed by what it is described as.
Classes too general to be a type (agent, physical object, system), unions of listed types (person or organization), Wikimedia-internal classes, and classes of classes (ship type).
Edge cases of the human class that do not appear as 2Wiki answers.
Names and words rather than the things they name.
Accounts, channels, services, voice banks, and AI models; none is a 2Wiki answer type.
excluded_constraint_classes.reason_key: online accounts, services, and software artefacts

classes.label: federally recognized Native American tribe in the United States

excluded_constraint_classes.reason: Ethnic groups, nations, nationality, and citizenship. Country of citizenship points at a Country in 2Wiki; these classes name the status, not the place.
Ships and astronomical places, listed as birth or detention places for rare cases.

name: 2Wiki treatment ontology

relation_types.definition: award or recognition received by a person, organization or creative work
relation_types.domain_note: P166 has no subject type constraint. Dev subjects are people and groups, e.g. 'Steve Vai' and 'Slayer' (Grammy Award).
relation_types.wikidata_description: award or recognition received by a person, organization or creative work

relation_types.definition: underlying or immediate cause of death
relation_types.wikidata_description: underlying or immediate cause of death. Underlying cause (e.g. car accident, stomach cancer) preferred. Use 'manner of death' (P1196) for broadest category, e.g. natural causes, accident, homicide, suicide

relation_types.definition: subject has object as child
relation_types.wikidata_description: subject has object as child. Do not use for stepchildren—use "relative" (P1038), qualified with "kinship to subject" (P1039)
